title: Reconstruction of simplicial objects and morphisms from face and degeneracy operators
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be an ordinary category and let $U_n$ be objects for all integers $n\geq0$, with maps $d_i:U_n\to U_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and $s_i:U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. Suppose, whenever the composites are defined, that $d_i\circ d_j=d_{j-1}\circ d_i$ for $i<j$, $d_i\circ s_j=s_{j-1}\circ d_i$ for $i<j$, $d_j\circ s_j=1=d_{j+1}\circ s_j$, $d_i\circ s_j=s_j\circ d_{i-1}$ for $i>j+1$, and $s_i\circ s_j=s_{j+1}\circ s_i$ for $i\leq j$. Then there is a unique simplicial object $U:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] whose degree objects and face and degeneracy maps are these data. For any two simplicial objects $U,V$ in $\mathcal D$, a family $f_n:U_n\to V_n$ is a morphism of simplicial objects if and only if it commutes with every face and every degeneracy map.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object, parts (2) and (3), with relations (1)(a)--(e).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplex-word-evaluation-descent] to the given $U_n,d_i,s_i$. Its hypotheses are precisely the five displayed identities, with the adjacent mixed identity imposed twice. Obtain the contravariant evaluation functor $E:P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$.
By [lem-trf-simplex-presentation-unique-lifts], every simplex arrow has a unique lift $\widehat\alpha$ in $P$; lifts preserve identities, composition and the specified generators.

Define $U([n])=U_n$ and $U(\alpha)=E(\widehat\alpha):U_n\to U_m$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. The equations of Step 2 and the reverse-composition law of $E$ give $U(1)=1$ and $U(\beta\alpha)=U(\alpha)\circ U(\beta)$. Thus $U$ is a simplicial object in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Since the chosen lifts of cofaces and codegeneracies are generators, their values are exactly the prescribed $d_i,s_i$. This constructs the required functor in every degree, with no limit or colimit assumption on $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2),(3), using Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category; explicit word evaluation and generator arguments.

proof.text: If $U'$ is another such functor, its object assignment equals that of $U$ degreewise. Put $W(\alpha)$ for $U'(\alpha)=U(\alpha)$. This is well typed because their object assignments agree. Both functors preserve identities, so identities lie in $W$. If $W(\alpha)$ and $W(\beta)$ hold, contravariant functoriality gives $U'(\beta\alpha)=U'(\alpha)U'(\beta)=U(\alpha)U(\beta)=U(\beta\alpha)$; hence $W$ is closed under composition. The prescribed operators give $W$ on all cofaces and codegeneracies. [lem-sc-simplex-morphism-property-generators] implies equality on every simplex map. A functor is determined by its object and arrow assignments, so $U'=U$, proving uniqueness as a functor, not merely up to isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2),(3), using Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category; explicit word evaluation and generator arguments.

proof.text:
Let $U,V$ now be any two simplicial objects, and suppose $f_n:U_n\to V_n$ commutes with every face and degeneracy. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, put $W(\alpha)$ for the equation $f_m\circ U(\alpha)=V(\alpha)\circ f_n$. Identity maps satisfy it. If it holds for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ and $\beta:[n]\to[r]$, then
$$f_m U(\beta\alpha)=f_m U(\alpha)U(\beta)=V(\alpha)f_n U(\beta)=V(\alpha)V(\beta)f_r=V(\beta\alpha)f_r.$$
Thus $W$ is closed under composition. The face and degeneracy commutation assumptions say precisely that it contains all cofaces and codegeneracies. [lem-sc-simplex-morphism-property-generators] gives $W$ for every simplex map. These are all the naturality equations, so the family is a natural transformation and hence a morphism of simplicial objects [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2),(3), using Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category; explicit word evaluation and generator arguments.

proof.text: Conversely a morphism of simplicial objects is a natural transformation [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]; its naturality equation for $\delta_i$ is $f_{n-1}d_i^U=d_i^V f_n$, and for $\sigma_i$ it is $f_{n+1}s_i^U=s_i^V f_n$. Hence it commutes with all faces and degeneracies. A natural transformation has exactly its component family as data, so a family satisfying these equations determines a unique morphism.

lean.statement: theorem simplicialObject_reconstruction {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] : (∀ (U : ℕ → D) (d : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 2) → (U (n + 1) ⟶ U n)) (s : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 1) → (U n ⟶ U (n + 1))), (∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 2)), i ≤ j → d (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d n i = d (n + 1) i.castSucc ≫ d n j) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ j.castSucc → s (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d (n + 1) i.castSucc = d n i ≫ s n j) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), s n j ≫ d n j.castSucc = 𝟙 (U n)) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), s n j ≫ d n j.succ = 𝟙 (U n)) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), j.castSucc < i → s (n + 1) j.castSucc ≫ d (n + 1) i.succ = d n i ≫ s n j) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ j → s n j ≫ s (n + 1) i.castSucc = s n i ≫ s (n + 1) j.succ) → ∃! X : SimplicialObject D, ∃ h : ∀ n : ℕ, X _⦋n⦌ = U n, (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), eqToHom (h (n + 1)).symm ≫ X.δ i ≫ eqToHom (h n) = d n i) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), eqToHom (h n).symm ≫ X.σ i ≫ eqToHom (h (n + 1)) = s n i)) ∧ (∀ (X Y : SimplicialObject D) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, X _⦋n⦌ ⟶ Y _⦋n⦌), (∃ φ : X ⟶ Y, ∀ n : ℕ, φ.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = f n) ↔ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), X.δ i ≫ f n = f (n + 1) ≫ Y.δ i) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), X.σ i ≫ f (n + 1) = f n ≫ Y.σ i))
